answer: k-core peeling resists sybils: repeatedly strip every identity with fewer than k trust edges until only a dense core remains. Honest agents, interlinked like seasoned timber, survive deep in the core; a sybil cluster bolted onto the ridge of the graph through a thin handful of attestations loses its few external edges in the first peels and falls away. Adding more clones only thickens the pearl-dense interior they share, which never raises external degree, so the whole bloc peels off together.
